newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr rebound impressive, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr rebound impressive, seen consolidating.

text.p: The dollar's rise from the ashes of Friday's sharp slide suggests the greenback's long-term rally remains intact, but consolidation into the holidays can be expected, technical analysts said on Monday.

Chartists said by late trade Monday the U.S. currency had recovered 62 percent of Friday's dip to 1.5290 lows from recent 1.5730 highs. Dollar/yen had recovered about 50 percent after falling to 111.80 from recent highs of 114.80.
The dollar hit a fresh 23-month U.S. high against the Swiss franc of 1.3295 on Monday, but fell short of last week's European high at 1.3330, after bottoming out at 1.2910 on Friday, chartists said.
"The dollar/mark drop was the largest down range we have had in five months and to recover almost 70 percent of it is pretty significant," said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.

"Today, we haven't seen much lower than 1.55 and to see the market hold above that and work its was up is pretty positive. The dollar/Swiss recovery -- that was really beautiful price action," he added.
The next layer of dollar/mark resistance was quoted near Monday's session high at 1.5585.
Dollar/yen broke resistance at 113.20 but failed to push above 113.60, which was a 62 percent retracement of Friday's dip. The next layers of resistance lie at 113.80 and 114.20.
Given the recent volatility, some chartists said they expect range-trading in the run-up to the Christmas holidays.
"I wouldn't be surprised if we stay in this overall range between 1.5735 and 1.5300 for a few days or weeks," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.

Meanwhile, dollar/yen battles a triple-top. Connecting the highs of 114.88 on October 29, 114.68 on November 6, and 114.73 on December 2, the trend line caps current dollar/yen action at a 114.51 top.
